_app_comment: The venv interpreter by path, not bare `python3`. On a pyenv-managed machine
`python3` resolves to a shim that is very often not this venv, so synth fails
with ModuleNotFoundError: aws_cdk even though pip install just succeeded here.
Same reasoning as the PYTHON resolution in fast/run.sh.

_group_comment: enforce_group is OFF by decision: anybody with a Cognito account in the pool
may use the roadmap. That pool is SHARED with the marketing compliance tool,
so this admits compliance-tool accounts too - which is the whole of what
allow_whole_pool is acknowledging. It was weighed and accepted: the pool holds
five people, all @qwealth.com, and the alternative was a group membership to
chase every time somebody new needed a date changed.
required_group is still named because /api/me reports it and the Cognito group
still exists; with enforcement off it is documentation. Setting enforce_group
back to true is the only change needed to make it bite again - nothing else
here or in the API depends on it being off.
admin_group is a DIFFERENT question and IS still enforced: it gates acting on
somebody other than yourself on the roster. 'admin' is the pool's existing
group, so a compliance-tool admin is an admin here too. Also deliberate.
Roadmap editing - projects, phases, milestones - stays open to everybody.
_dns_comment: planning.qconnect.qwnext.com nests inside an ALREADY-DELEGATED zone, which
is the only reason this is safe. `dig +short NS qconnect.qwnext.com
@8.8.8.8` returns four Route53 nameservers. Do NOT change domain_name to a
first-level subdomain of qwnext.com: that apex is served by Cloudflare, the
Route53 zone named qwnext.com is vestigial, and a new name there needs a
Cloudflare NS record that AWS credentials cannot create. intake.qwnext.com
and onboarding.qwnext.com are the cautionary tale - zones that resolve
nowhere and six ACM certs dead of VALIDATION_TIMED_OUT.
Set domain_name to null to deploy the API alone with no cert and no record.
_cors_comment: The browser reaches /api/* on the SAME origin, through CloudFront, so normal
use triggers no preflight and needs nothing here. The custom domain is listed
anyway for the case that does cross origins: a Vite dev server on :5173
_service_caller_comment: IAM roles allowed to call /api/service/*, which is the ONLY door into this API
that is not a signed-in human. Today that is the Aardvark Aap Slack bot, whose
/roadmap-invite command creates logins on the Cognito pool SHARED with the
That command is gated by Aardvark's OWN admin list, in its MySQL `admins`
table - not by the `admin` Cognito group this app uses everywhere else. So
this line delegates account creation to a permission set maintained in another
system, and it is written out here so that decision is reviewable in this repo
rather than only in Aardvark's CDK.
Matched on the ROLE, so the assumed-role session suffix ECS regenerates on
every task does not matter. Empty or absent closes the door entirely.
The matching grant - execute-api:Invoke - lives in aardvarkaap/lib/
aardvark-app-stack.ts. Both sides are required; neither alone does anything.
_slack_comment: Aardvark Aap's Slack credentials, read by the invite picker on the Team page.
SHARED with Aardvark rather than copied: one Slack app, one bot token, rotated
in one place. The consequence is that a DM sent by this app appears to come
from Aardvark, which matches its own /roadmap-invite command.
This app is granted GetSecretValue on this ONE secret and nothing else - see
lib/lambda_stack.py, which also explains the -?????? suffix every Secrets
Manager ARN carries. The token is never put in a Lambda environment variable.
The Slack app needs users:read, users:read.email and chat:write, and must be
REINSTALLED to the workspace after any scope is added. Set this to "" to turn
the picker off; inviting by typed address keeps working either way.
